overridableConfigKeys.label: Mode
overridableConfigKeys.description: Which history simulation to render: a WWI causal-chain counterfactual graph, or a Fall-of-Rome periodization timeline.
overridableConfigKeys.synonyms: history, historical causation, cause and effect, causal chain, counterfactual, counterfactual history, structural cause, proximate cause, trigger, casus belli, alliance system, militarism, nationalism, imperialism, imperial rivalry, assassination, Franz Ferdinand, WWI, World War One, First World War, July Crisis, timeline, periodization, fall of Rome, decline of Rome, Western Roman Empire, historiography, primary source lens, historical lens

overridableConfigKeys.default: Taken together, the threads reinforce each other — political fragmentation weakens defense, military defeat costs territory and revenue, and fiscal collapse starves the state of the resources reform would need. No single lens tells the whole story.

default.summary: Viewed through politics alone, Rome's fall is administrative: civil war, reform, and a permanent East-West split hollow out central authority long before any emperor is deposed.
Viewed through the military alone, Rome's fall is a string of defeats and incursions — Adrianople, two sacks of the capital, endless frontier pressure — that leave the West unable to defend itself.
Viewed through economics alone, Rome's fall is fiscal: the loss of North Africa's tax base and decades of currency debasement starve the state of resources that war and administration both require.

default.description: Decades of civil war and rapid emperor turnover near-collapse central authority across the Empire.
default.label: Crisis of the Third Century Begins

default.description: The Empire is split into a Tetrarchy and its administration overhauled to stabilize imperial control.
default.label: Diocletian's Reforms

default.description: Diocletian tries to halt runaway inflation from decades of currency debasement, with limited success.
default.label: Edict on Maximum Prices

default.description: Fleeing the Huns, the Goths are admitted into Roman territory, straining military and food supply.
default.label: Goths Cross the Danube

default.description: A Roman field army is destroyed by Gothic forces, a catastrophic blow exposing imperial vulnerability.
default.label: Battle of Adrianople

default.description: Theodosius's sons divide administration; East and West never again reunite under one emperor.
default.label: Empire Permanently Splits East and West

default.description: The city of Rome is sacked for the first time in 800 years, a profound symbolic and military shock.
default.label: Sack of Rome by Alaric

default.description: Rome loses its wealthiest grain-producing province in North Africa, crippling tax revenue and food supply.
default.label: Vandals Seize Carthage

default.description: A Roman-led coalition halts Attila's Huns, but the effort further drains dwindling military resources.
default.label: Battle of the Catalaunian Plains

default.description: A second sack of Rome underscores the collapse of Western military capacity to defend the capital.
default.label: Vandals Sack Rome

default.description: Odoacer deposes the last Western emperor; conventionally marked as the fall of the Western Roman Empire.
default.label: Romulus Augustulus Deposed
